subject: DI03000091

body.en:
Understand the idea

Measurement compares a quantity with a defined reference;state the measurand,unit,method and conditions.

Explanation and application

  • Direct:a suitable instrument displays the desired quantity,for example a voltmeter reading voltage.Indirect:derive it from other measured quantities,for example R=V/I.
  • Indirect measurement carries the uncertainty and loading errors of every input.In a V/Iresistance test,the actual ammeter/voltmeter connection changes the correction needed.
  • Areading is not a true value merely because a digital display shows many digits.Resolution,calibration and uncertainty must support the reported precision.
Error versus correction?

e=Xi−Xr;c=−e.

Understand the idea

Classify by the measurement task and method,not just analogue versus digital appearance.

Explanation and application

  • Indicating instruments show an instantaneous/quasi-steady reading;integrating instruments accumulate a quantity over time,for example kWh;recording instruments retain its time history.
  • Absolute instruments determine quantity from physical constants/dimensions and observed response;secondary instruments use prior calibration and a graduated scale/display.
  • An energy meter measures energy,not power;an indicating wattmeter gives power and a demand meter reports power over a stated interval.

Understand the idea

Follow the quantity from the physical process to the person or controller using the result.

Explanation and application

  • Primary sensing element responds to the measurand;conversion changes it into a suitable signal;conditioning may amplify,filter,linearise or isolate.
  • Transmission carries the signal to display/recording/data acquisition.Areference/excitation source is required for many passive sensors.
  • Each stage has its own range,bandwidth,loading and error;an accurate display cannot repair an unsuitable sensor or saturated amplifier.

Understand the idea

Amechanical pointer needs a driving torque,a position-dependent restoring torque and controlled settling.

Explanation and application

  • Deflecting torque Tdcomes from the measured electrical quantity and moves the pointer.Controlling torque Tcfrom a spring or gravity opposes deflection and defines the final equilibrium.
  • At rest Td=Tc.For a linear spring Tc=kθ.Without control the pointer would move to a stop rather than indicate a unique value.
  • Damping torque opposes motion and ideally vanishes at rest;air/fluid friction or eddy-current arrangements reduce oscillation.It does not establish the final calibrated reading.
  • Underdamped response oscillates;overdamping settles slowly;near-critical damping gives quick settling without sustained oscillation.

Understand the idea

State the reference and sign convention before quoting an error.

Explanation and application

  • Range is the interval covered;span=upper−lower limit.Indicated value is the displayed result;a reference value has its own uncertainty and is not necessarily exact truth.
  • Error e=indication−reference;correction c=−e=reference−indication.Relative error=e/reference,when reference is nonzero.Percent-of-reading and percent-of-full-scale are different bases.
  • Sensitivity=change of output/change of input around the specified operating point.Resolution is the smallest distinguishable change,not accuracy or sensitivity.
  • Example:indication102V,reference100V gives error+2V,correction−2V,relative error+2%.On a200Vfull-scale instrument that same error is+1%of full scale.

Understand the idea

Repeatable results can still all be biased;do not confuse consistency with closeness to a reference.

Explanation and application

  • Accuracy concerns closeness to a reference;precision concerns agreement among repeated values under stated conditions.Calibration helps identify bias,not automatically eliminate random scatter.
  • Repeatability uses the same method,operator,instrument and conditions over a short interval.Reproducibility changes specified conditions such as operator,location or equipment.
  • Report significant figures supported by resolution/uncertainty;do not retain calculator digits that imply nonexistent measurement quality.

Understand the idea

Identify a cause before choosing a correction or statistical method.

Explanation and application

  • Gross errors include misreading,wrong range,wrong units or transcription mistakes;prevent them with checks and valid procedures.Do not simply average a known mistake into the result.
  • Systematic errors have a consistent pattern:zero offset,scale/calibration bias,temperature effects or loading.They may need correction or a better method.
  • Random error produces unpredictable scatter.Repetition and statistical analysis can estimate its spread,but averaging does not remove systematic bias.

Understand the idea

The instrument becomes part of the circuit it measures.

Explanation and application

  • Avoltmeter with finite input resistance loads the source.An ammeter adds burden resistance/voltage;their ideal values are infinite and zero resistance respectively.
  • Other sources include leads/contact resistance,thermal EMFs,parallax,wrong mounting position,temperature,humidity,stray fields,supply frequency and waveform.
  • Example:a10VThevenin source with10kΩsource resistance and10kΩvoltmeter input reads5V;the source was loaded,not suddenly a5Vsource.

Understand the idea

Combine sensor,conditioning,power/reference,display and decision functions for the real application.

Explanation and application

  • Choose range,uncertainty,response time,environment,signal interface and fail-safe behaviour for the actual process;the cheapest single component may not give a usable system.
  • CTsecondary must not be opened while primary current flows;PTsecondary must not be shorted.Insulation/earth tests require isolation,approved test voltage and discharge.
  • CAT/voltage/current ratings,leads,fuses and approved earthing matter;low indicated voltage does not prove a circuit safe.Qualified-supervised power-lab work only.

title.en: Practical.1 Identify dial symbols,range,class and position
title.gu: Practical.1 Dial Symbols,Range,Class તથા Position ઓળખો

body.en:
Aim and apparatus

Identify dial symbols,range,class and position

Use the approved rated trainer,instruments/references and manufacturer manual;no physical experiment is claimed.

Connections and instruments

Inspect de-energised instruments and their manuals;identify terminals,principle,AC/DCmark,class,range,scale and operating position.

Qualified-supervised procedure

  1. Identify ratings,ranges,terminals,test conditions and stop criteria;prepare an approved diagram and reference/uncertainty plan.
  2. Isolate and verify dead before setup;inspect earthing,protection,guards and leads.Never bypass protection or rewire live.
  3. Inspect de-energised instruments and their manuals;identify terminals,principle,AC/DCmark,class,range,scale and operating position.
  4. Prepare a genuine identification table for each available instrument;separate smallest division,resolution and stated class.
  5. Record only actual readings with units,conditions and uncertainty;leave unperformed observations blank and keep expected calculations separate.
  6. Follow the approved shutdown,discharge and dead-verification procedure before access or reconnection;CT/PTand earth/insulation work require the specific authorised precautions.

Calculations and interpretation

If a class is expressed against fiducial value,apply only that declared base;do not assume percent-of-reading.

Safe fault-finding

Missing/unclear symbols require manual/instructor confirmation,not guessed live connections.

Precautions

No CTsecondary open under primary current;no PTsecondary short;no arbitrary insulation voltage or defeated earth.Scope grounds remain PE/common;never lift PEor float an earthed scope.Use approved rated differential/isolated-input methods if needed.

Actual record — blank
